agent instructions.definition: Rules for a person or agent working on the project.

anchor region.definition: The Markdown lines belonging to a particular explicit anchor.

approach.definition: The method chosen to carry out a plan.

architecture decision.definition: A record of a decision, its context, and its consequences.

audit.definition: An examination of a project and the findings it produced.

baseline.definition: A recorded set of existing errors used to identify new errors.

check code.definition: The stable identifier of a check, such as D1.

closure log.definition: The index of closed work grouped by closure year.

code location.definition: A file and line identifying code relevant to a target.

conclusions.definition: The judgments reached from the available evidence.

connected repository.definition: A neighboring repository explicitly listed in project settings.

consequences.definition: The effects expected from adopting a decision.

context.definition: The circumstances that explain why a decision was needed.

discussion.definition: A work item for exploring a question before deciding.

document header.definition: The structured fields below a document’s title.

entry point.definition: A configured location where a user or caller enters the code.

excerpt.definition: The portion of a target displayed in a slice.

exit code.definition: The numeric result returned by a command to its caller.

explicit anchor.definition: A stable identifier written explicitly in Markdown.

facts.definition: Observations used as evidence in a discussion or audit.

finding.definition: A condition reported by a project check.

findings.definition: The results of an examination that call for attention.

fingerprint.definition: A content digest used to detect a change in a source.

how to reproduce or where it occurred.definition: The steps or circumstances that demonstrate an issue.
how to reproduce or where it occurred.term: how to reproduce or where it occurred

issue.definition: A recorded bug, friction, request, or question.

language edition.definition: One language’s version of a set of documentation pages.

layer.definition: A project-defined grouping of code paths.

map.definition: A table of explicit trace coverage across targets, layers, and tests.

master plan.definition: The project’s ordered queue of approved work.

options.definition: The alternatives considered before a decision.

plan.definition: A work item that sets out steps and completion criteria.

project documentation.definition: Pages that describe the project’s current behavior and rules.

question and scope.definition: The question under examination and the limits of that examination.

review mark.definition: A recorded review of a code and documentation pair, valid while both fingerprints match.

section.definition: An addressable part of a documentation page.

signal.definition: An item that may affect how a change should be made.

slice.definition: A focused view of the documents, code, tests, and signals for a target or change.

staleness.definition: A possible mismatch when related code is newer than its documentation.

steps.definition: The ordered actions that make up a plan.

target.definition: The page, anchor, work item, or code file addressed by a query or reference.

trace marker.definition: An explicit annotation connecting code or tests to a target.

trace marker group.definition: The longest run of adjacent lines with stand-alone trace markers; a line with code and a trace marker forms its own group.

trace region.definition: A trace marker group together with the text up to the next group or the end of the file.

work item.definition: A numbered item that can be referenced by its identifier.

workflow document.definition: One numbered document within the workflow.

workflow documents.definition: Files used to record work, decisions, discussions, and audits.
